name: Cups are symmetric
summary: A cup followed by a swap is the cup (and likewise for the cap).
description:
Swapping the two legs of a cup gives the cup back; upside down, the same holds for the cap. This is the axiom $com$ of Hadzihasanovic's ZW-calculus, which makes the compact structure *symmetric*. It holds in the ZX-, ZH- and ZW-calculus alike, and is built into PyZX and ZXLive, where only connectivity matters.

The swap here is an ordinary swap of wires, not the fermionic crossing of the ZW-calculus.
unchecked_reason: bare cups and caps cannot be represented with ZXLive-style boundaries

source.location: Chapter 5, Section 5.2 (list of rules of the ZW calculus), rule $com$
